title: Hosted API request fencing + surgical rollback telemetry shim for escalations
creator: Aisha Rao
description:
Summary:
During multiple customer escalations last quarter we observed correlated 5xx/timeouts originating from tenant migration windows. Symptoms: rapid retry amplification, large fanout from front-door to inference pool, KV cache thrashing and connection hold. Existing mitigations (soft-quarantine, adaptive backoff) reduced surface area but did not prevent noisy tenant retries from causing multi-tenant collateral damage.

Root cause hypothesis:
- Client SDKs and customers issue aggressive retries when p50 latency spikes; many retries replay identical semantic requests.
- Edge/front-proxy currently lacks a cheap way to detect replayed requests vs unique requests (no per-request fencing token).
- During migrations/failovers the runtime sometimes returns transient 5xx; client retries then cause downstream amplification and KV cache churn.

Proposed solution (high level): request-fencing + surgical rollback telemetry shim
1) Request fencing: generate an opaque fence token at the edge (derived from tenant id, time-window, and request fingerprint) and attach as X-RW-Fence header. Backends validate the fence and deduplicate replays within a short window (e.g., 10s). The goal is to convert retry storms into fast-failures or single-processing paths without adding heavy coordination.
2) Fast fallback route: when fence validation fails or runtime returns repeated 5xx for a tenant, edge routing will automatically route that tenant's traffic to a pre-provisioned fallback pool (lower-capacity dedicated variant or a degraded model) via feature-flag-controlled policy. This is a surgical rollback path that avoids full code rollback.
3) Telemetry shim: add lightweight tracing anchors and per-fence counters at edge + runtime to measure amplification, fence hit/miss, and per-tenant retry ratios. Surface these in a Grafana dashboard and a Slack alert for >5x amplification.
4) Operator controls: feature-flagging and per-tenant fast-path toggle in Console (UI + API) to temporarily fence or route a tenant away from shared pools during escalations without deployment rollback.

Why this is different: the approach focuses on distinguishing replayed retries at the edge (cheaply) and providing an operator-accessible rollback path that is deployment-agnostic. This reduces blast radius and gives SREs a fast, low-risk tool during active escalations.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not implement long-term cross-tenant KV sync (future work).
- We will not change client SDK retry semantics in this effort (SDK changes are separate).
acceptance_criteria: Edge attaches X-RW-Fence header to >=99% of incoming hosted API requests in test canary
Runtime deduplicates repeated requests with identical fence token within 10s window and returns a 429 or cached response as configured
Per-tenant amplification metric computed and visible in Grafana (panel + alert) - alert fires on >5x amplification for 2 minutes
Canary rollback routing can be toggled from Console for a tenant and route changes take effect within 30s
Runbook steps documented and smoke-tested (post-deploy) with SRE sign-off
work_notes: 2026-03-01 - Triage: Observed multi-tenant 5xx spikes during major customer migration window. Assigned ENG-827463 to implement a short-lived mitigation that prevents retry amplification without code rollback. (Aisha)

2026-03-02 - Spike: Implemented PoC fence token generator at edge (node/proxy) and simple dedupe map in runtime worker. PoC shows 60-80% reduction in duplicate request processing in replay tests. Created spike PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4567 (Samir)

2026-03-04 - Review: Security review queued - token design uses HMAC with short TTL; avoids PII. Preliminary design doc added to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Request+Fencing+Design (Aisha)

2026-03-05 - Instrumentation: Added per-fence metrics (fence.accepted, fence.duplicate, fence.missed) and retry_amplification.per_tenant. Dashboard skeleton: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/tenant-fence/tenant-retries (Samir)

2026-03-07 - Hotfix release: Merged runtime dedupe and edge header injection behind feature flags. Deployed to us-west-2 canary (1% of traffic). Observed immediate drop in processed tokens for synthetic retry storms. Hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4598

2026-03-09 - Operator controls: Console API endpoint /admin/tenants/:id/fallback-route implemented (internal-only). UI piece scheduled in console-2026.03 sprint. Added canary-playbook runbook: https://docs.redwood.ai/runbooks/request-fence-canary.md

2026-03-10 - Partial rollout: Expanded canary to 10% traffic. Noted two tenants with >10% amplification despite fencing; investigating KV cache TTL interactions. Follow-up task created: ENG-827464 (KV cache TTL tuning for fenced requests).
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Incorrect fence token collisions could cause legitimate requests to be dropped. Mitigation: HMAC with tenant-scoped nonce and 10s TTL; conservative default is to return 429 with retry-after when deduped, not 5xx.
Risk: Additional latency for header signing. Mitigation: implement efficient HMAC and cache keys at edge; measured <0.8ms median overhead in PoC.
Risk: SRE unfamiliarity with new operator controls. Mitigation: runbook + playbook run with on-call and pager duty rehearsals scheduled during canary.
Risk: KV cache TTL interaction producing false misses. Mitigation: follow-up task ENG-827464 to align KV eviction and fence windows.
postmortem_actions: Document findings in postmortem and mark any residual impacted tenants for follow-up
Add fence token telemetry to long-term retention for 90 days (product decision) if it proves useful
Parallel effort: coordinate with SDK owners to optionally add client-side fence propagation in next major SDK release
Close follow-ups: ENG-827464 (KV tuning), ENG-827470 (console UI for per-tenant rollback)
Schedule brown-bag with SRE/Support to walk through new operator controls
